# socketley

> One Linux daemon and CLI that runs your servers, proxies, caches, storage, databases, DNS, sign-in, MQTT, mail, metrics, tunnels and MCP: each a runtime made with one command.

socketley is a single Linux binary. `socketley daemon` supervises runtimes; every other invocation is the CLI that talks to the daemon over a unix socket. A runtime is a network service of one of 14 types, made with `socketley create <type> <name> [flags]`, each in its own worker process on an io_uring event loop, scriptable in Lua. The manual page man/socketley.1 is the source of truth; these files are generated from it and from the site's own pages (https://docs.smileygames.online/).

Every page below is plain Markdown. llms-full.txt is all of them in one file (large).

## Start

- [socketley](llms/index.txt): One Linux daemon and CLI that runs your servers, proxies, caches, storage, databases, DNS, sign-in, MQTT, mail, metrics, tunnels and MCP: each a runtime made with one command.
- [Install](llms/install.txt): From source, the install script or a Debian package; the daemon then runs as a systemd service.
- [Ten-minute tour](llms/tour.txt): Make a server, a cache and a proxy, script one of them, and look at all three.
- [Concepts](llms/concepts.txt): The daemon, its runtimes and the few rules every one of them follows.
- [How it works](llms/how.txt): What happens, and where, from the command you type to the answer a client gets.

## Runtimes

- [server runtime](llms/rt-server.txt): TCP, UDP, WebSocket and HTTP on one port, answered by Lua or by a built-in path
- [client runtime](llms/rt-client.txt): Dials a server and holds the connection: TCP, UDP or a unix socket, over TLS, reconnecting
- [proxy runtime](llms/rt-proxy.txt): HTTP and TCP reverse proxy: routes by name and path, health checks, retries, mTLS, FastCGI
- [cache runtime](llms/rt-cache.txt): In-memory store on the Redis protocol: strings, lists, sets, hashes, sorted sets, streams, pub/sub
- [storage runtime](llms/rt-storage.txt): S3 object storage over a directory, with versioning, replication, a web drive and git
- [db runtime](llms/rt-db.txt): JSON documents owned by accounts, over HTTP, with indexes, queries, replicas and backups
- [dns runtime](llms/rt-dns.txt): Authoritative name server for its zones, over UDP and TCP, with DNSSEC and transfers
- [idp runtime](llms/rt-idp.txt): OpenID Connect provider with its own accounts, second factors, app passwords and SSH certificates
- [mail runtime](llms/rt-mail.txt): Mail server: SMTP, submission, IMAP, POP3, JMAP and webmail, mailboxes in a storage
- [mqtt runtime](llms/rt-mqtt.txt): MQTT 3.1, 3.1.1 and 5.0 broker on TCP, TLS and WebSocket, with sessions and rules
- [metrics runtime](llms/rt-metrics.txt): Time series for years, answered with PromQL over the Prometheus API, with alert rules and logs
- [sync runtime](llms/rt-sync.txt): One job that carries a directory to a storage, from it, or both ways
- [tunnel runtime](llms/rt-tunnel.txt): Makes a machine without an address of its own reachable through an edge it dials
- [mcp runtime](llms/rt-mcp.txt): A Model Context Protocol server: the tools, resources and prompts its script declares, for AI clients

## Guides

- [Lua scripting](llms/lua.txt): Callbacks per message, connection and request, the runtime methods a script calls, and what a script may not do.
- [Deployment](llms/deploy.txt): Running socketley on a machine that matters: the service, permissions, TLS, state, backups and limits.
- [Cluster](llms/cluster.txt): Daemons on several machines that see each other's runtimes, and the opt-in Raft mode.
- [C++ SDK](llms/sdk.txt): Control a daemon, embed the engine, or attach a process of your own to a daemon.
- [Examples](llms/examples.txt): Every script and program in examples/ and sdk/examples/.

## Reference

- [CLI](llms/cli.txt): Every command socketley takes, with its options.
- [All flags](llms/flags.txt): Every flag of every runtime type, with the types that take it.
- [Environment & files](llms/env.txt): The variables the daemon and the CLI read, and where everything lives on disk.
- [Benchmarks](llms/bench.txt): Each runtime against what people run instead, on one machine, in one run.
